chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That he disliked that the polytheist be fed from the meat of the sacrificial animals.

key_terms.الْمُشْرِك: Polytheist, one who associates partners with God
key_terms.كَرِهَ: He disliked (expressing a preferred dislike, not prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams dislike giving sacrificial meat to polytheists?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expressed dislike (karahah) for feeding polytheists the meat of udhiyah, distinguishing this specific sacrificial offering from general charity. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that while polytheists may receive general zakat or sadaqah, the specific ritual meat of udhiyah carries a higher status of purity and exclusivity, often reserved for Muslims to emphasize communal identity. The context of Chapter 25 in Tahdhib al-Ahkam links this etiquette to the broader principles of expiation and ritual conditions, highlighting the importance of proper distribution in maintaining ritual integrity.
